test_vectors.assertions: Shared backing is Exact; full, sliced, and empty Bytes backing is AtLeast. Visible counts and minimum/exact totals match.
A reserved arena reports logical lengths 0, 6, 3, and 0 while retaining capacity. Totals use capacity, and unknown payload backing prevents an exact total.
Accounting leaves Arc strong counts unchanged and is independent of other owners.
Exact and AtLeast u64::MAX backing exercise saturating minimum totals and checked exact totals with decoded capacities 0 and 1.

Twelve explicit vectors run against both ownership variants. Covers zero and positive savings, below/equal/above thresholds, forced visible-budget copying, unknown-backing policy, rebasing, variant preservation, and exact compacted accounting.
A 4097-byte Shared owner retains two selected bytes without copying at 4095 bytes saved, and copies one selected byte at exactly 4096 bytes saved.
The body span (7,4) in prefix:body:suffix preserves Arc identity and adds exactly one owner; into_payload returns all 17 bytes and the saved span still resolves.
A Bytes slice exposing body resolves span (1,2) as od, preserves its visible range and pointer, remains AtLeast(4), and survives dropping the input.
Full, partial, and empty selections from sliced Bytes become independent Shared owners with Exact selected lengths when copy_unknown_backing is enabled.
Zero budgets and zero thresholds do not copy empty known backing; empty unknown backing copies only when requested.
Empty spans at offsets 0, 5, and 13 in a 13-byte owner compact under a zero budget without retaining the original Arc.

Out-of-bounds and overflowing spans produce canonical InvalidToken/Decode errors before budget validation. Valid over-budget selections produce BudgetExhausted/Decode at their original offsets. All error metadata and input identity are asserted.

Length-only production validation covers zero, u32::MAX, full and end-empty ABI spans, overflowing ends, selected-budget failure, and oversized usize lengths where representable. PayloadTooLarge precedes span and budget failures.

3528 deterministic cases span every subrange of five binary bytes, both storage variants, budgets 0 through 6, six savings thresholds, and both unknown-backing flags. Each success is also resolved through OwnerBytes.

A 24-byte admitted Bytes payload and a decoded arena hold a 10-byte, four-scalar Unicode value. Compaction rebases (7,10) to (0,10), checked string views accept the rebased reference and reject old coordinates, original owners remain unchanged, and a retained clone survives their destruction.
Compaction preserves partial UTF-8, NUL, invalid UTF-8 bytes, and a literal JSON surrogate escape without content validation.
Successive copies from body to od record coordinates relative to each immediate owner. A subsequent zero-savings Shared retention preserves storage and outlives all earlier owners.
